## Motivation

A null or empty value in a `--config` YAML file reaches argparse as the literal string `None`, because `ConfigArgumentMerger._convert_config_to_args` passes it through `str()`. String flags accept that silently, and int flags stop the server with an error that does not point at the config file.

Results from `prepare_server_args(["--config", ...])` on `main` and on this branch:

| `config.yaml` line | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api-key: null` or `api-key:` | `api_key='None'` | `api_key=None` |
| `tokenizer-path: null` | `tokenizer_path='None'` | `tokenizer_path=None` |
| `chat-template: ~` | `chat_template='None'` | `chat_template=None` |
| `context-length: null` | exits with `argument --context-length: Invalid integer value: 'None'` | `context_length=None` |

The `api-key` row matters most. Someone who writes `api-key: null` to leave auth off gets auth turned on with the key `None`: a request with no key is rejected, and `Authorization: Bearer None` is accepted.

I checked the open PRs that touch this file, and none of them handle null values.

## Modifications

- `_convert_config_to_args` skips null values, so the flag behaves as if it were not in the file and keeps its default. Unsupported keys are still checked first, so they raise as before.
- Add a regression test next to the existing `--config` test in `test_server_args.py`. It covers string and int flags, all three YAML spellings of null, and a flag with a non-null default.
- Document the behavior in `server_arguments.mdx`.

This only changes top-level values. A null inside a list is unchanged, and nested mappings already go through `json.dumps`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This change only affects CLI argument parsing.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This change only runs once at startup.

## Verification

All of this ran on CPU, with no server launched and no GPU used:

- The new test fails on `main` with the `--context-length` error above and passes with the fix.
- `test/registered/unit/server_args`: 468 passed, 1 failed on this branch, and 467 passed, 1 failed on `main`. The same test fails with the same error on both: `TestMultimodalFeatureTransport::test_default_transport_is_cpu_for_unsupported_multinode_model`. On `main` it passes when run alone, so it is unrelated to this change.
- `pre-commit run --files` passes on the three changed files. I did not run `--all-files`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable, see above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -11,7 +11,7 @@ You can find all arguments by `python3 -m sglang.launch_server --help`
 
 ## Common launch commands
 
-- To use a configuration file, create a YAML file with your server arguments and specify it with `--config`. CLI arguments will override config file values.
+- To use a configuration file, create a YAML file with your server arguments and specify it with `--config`. CLI arguments will override config file values. A key set to `null` or left empty is treated as unset, so that argument keeps its default.
 
   ```bash Command
   # Create config.yaml

@@ -171,6 +171,9 @@ def _convert_config_to_args(self, config: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[str]:
                 action = self.unsupported_actions[key_norm]
                 msg = f"Unsupported config option '{key_norm}' with action '{action.__class__.__name__}'"
                 raise ValueError(msg)
+            # argparse has no spelling for None; str(None) would set the literal "None".
+            if value is None:
+                continue
             if isinstance(value, bool):
                 self._add_boolean_arg(args, key, value)
             elif isinstance(value, list):

@@ -985,6 +985,32 @@ def test_config_nested_dict_args_are_json(self):
         finally:
             os.unlink(config_file)
 
+    def test_config_null_values_leave_args_unset(self):
+        """A YAML null must not reach a flag as the literal string "None"."""
+        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", suffix=".yaml", delete=False) as f:
+            f.write("api-key: null\ntokenizer-path:\ncontext-length: ~\nport: null\n")
+            config_file = f.name
+
+        try:
+            parser = server_args_module.argparse.ArgumentParser()
+            ServerArgs.add_cli_args(parser)
+            merged = ConfigArgumentMerger(parser).merge_config_with_args(
+                [
+                    "--config",
+                    config_file,
+                    "--model-path",
+                    DEFAULT_SMALL_MODEL_NAME_FOR_TEST_QWEN,
+                ]
+            )
+            parsed = parser.parse_args(merged)
+
+            self.assertIsNone(parsed.api_key)
+            self.assertIsNone(parsed.tokenizer_path)
+            self.assertIsNone(parsed.context_length)
+            self.assertEqual(parsed.port, parser.get_default("port"))
+        finally:
+            os.unlink(config_file)
+
